implementation_constraints: reads one JSON value from stdin, prints one line, exits 0

unresolved_intent.decision: reject booleans as priority values even though bool is a Python int subclass
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec says priority is <int>; silently accepting true/false as 1/0 would let malformed-looking input slip through as valid, so this compiler treats bool priority as malformed -> ERROR

unresolved_intent.decision: treat an explicit `needs: null` the same as an absent needs field (no dependencies)
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec only defines 'needs may be absent = no dependencies' and doesn't address explicit null; treating null as equivalent to absent is the least surprising reading and avoids spuriously rejecting otherwise well-formed jobs

unresolved_intent.decision: alternate between running all currently-ready jobs and, only when none are ready, cascading skipped status to jobs blocked by a failed/skipped dependency, repeating to a fixpoint
unresolved_intent.rationale: the spec doesn't spell out the interleaving of execution vs. skip-propagation; this order guarantees every job ends decided (ok/failed/skipped) for any acyclic, validated graph and keeps 'order' exactly the executed jobs in run order

unresolved_intent.decision: select the ready job via max() over the ready list built in original input order, using priority as the sole key
unresolved_intent.rationale: Python's max() keeps the first maximal element on ties when iterating a stably-ordered list, which reproduces 'highest priority, then FIFO by input order' without a separate stable-sort step

unresolved_intent.decision: emit a plain json.dumps of {"order":..., "status":...} with default separators/key order, no pretty-printing
unresolved_intent.rationale: spec states output formatting is free and only structure/values are fixed, so no canonicalization beyond valid JSON is attempted

compilation_report.constraint_handling: r2: second blind run of the same model on the same canonical package (ADR-027 intra-model variance)
